input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
input.rationale:
Despite the one-sided heading, Section 15's operative text is mutual: each party's remedy is limited to direct damages, neither party is liable for indirect/consequential damages, and the limitation is expressly disapplied for breaches of Section 13 (IP ownership/warranty and Garman's indemnity for "Losses" at p0090) and Section 14 (confidentiality). No monetary cap exists anywhere in the agreement, so Garman's direct-damages exposure is unlimited and the IP indemnity and confidentiality obligations sit outside the limitation - a position more favourable to us than the preferred greater-of-12-months'-fees/USD 1,000,000 cap and symmetric between the parties. No walk-away trigger applies. Noted but not flagged: our own direct-damages liability is likewise uncapped (we would not introduce a mutual cap, as that would cap Garman's exposure and reduce our recovery), and gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud are not separately named carve-outs, which affects only the mutual consequential-damages exclusion.</rationale>
